content:
Just a heads up that I have begun the process of upstreaming the Wiener-Ikehara theorem (and the WeakPNT) corollary) to Mathlib. This will take some time: the 2700+ lines of code in PNT+ needed to get to WeakPNT was not designed with Mathlib upstreamability in mind. Initially I am proceeding by identifying pieces of the proof that are independently upstreamable and PR'ing those: see #42932 #42933 #42953. This (together with some identification of redundancy of old code with new Mathlib additions) has already reduced the remaining amount of code to upstream to about 2200 lines of code, but there is clearly still a ways to go. Will post updates when there is more to report. (In the unlikely chance that anyone is interested in the process, the draft code is at https://github.com/teorth/mathlib4/tree/wiener-ikehara .)

UPDATE: now down to 1674 lines, as my coding agent has identified a redundancy in the summability of a certain function fun n ↦ ‖f n‖ / n * (C / (1 + (log (n / x) / (2 * π)) ^ 2)), and a bound on its value, were proven separately using two different proofs, but the agent was able to find a common proof which established both.

Update: Now at 1288 lines. A large part of prior code was devoted to showing that a Schwartz function could be approximated in W^{2,1} norm by a test function. The more useful statement that test functions are in fact dense in Schwartz space has now been spun off at #43046, and all the W^{2,1} material could then be removed.

The branch is now stable: the Wiener-Ikehara theorem is golfed down to 718 lines (plus a lot of supporting API that is currently spread out over six other PRs to Mathlib), and the applications to the weak prime number theorem (in various forms), plus the weak PNT in arithmetic progressions, in a second file with 273 lines. Given all the dependencies I'll probably wait until most of the precursor PRs go through before submitting a PR for Wiener-Ikehara and then Weak PNT, but there is a clear path to getting everything into Mathilb.

One key structural change was to make a WienerIkehara class that bundles all the running hypotheses of the Wiener-Ikehara theorem. By working inside that namespace and declaring an instance of that class as a variable, one gets access to all the data and hypotheses in that class without any dot notation or explicit naming of the class variable, which is convenient.

Many of the sublemmas involving test functions were formulated in a way that kept regularity or decay conditions on the test function cutoff to a minimum, but it ends up being cleaner to just work with SchwartzMap functions throughout; this weakens the generality of some of the private lemmas used to prove the Wiener-Ikehara theorem, but they would be unlikely to be reusable in any event.

WeakPNT is now PR'ed to Mathlib as #43238 ; 1381 lines of code, spread out over 10 separate PRs, of which the largest is the Wiener-Ikehara PR #43233 (718 lines of code). We'll see how this survives the Mathlib review process. (The Mertens PR #41934 (1380 lines of code) is still held up, in part due to the need to review the precursor PR #41120 (91 lines of code) that (among other things) provides an integral formula for the Euler-Mascheroni constant.)

The two pre-requisite PR's for Mertens are now merged. I will coordinate reviewing of the Mertens PR, which has been split into 3 pieces. I will post links to them here, one-per-message so that the CI-status bot will post status updates as emojis. (Green tick means "passes tests"; writing hand means "someone left comments".)

  • #44061 feat(NumberTheory/Mertens): abstract theory of Mertens weights
• #44062 feat(NumberTheory/Mertens): construction of the prime and von Mangoldt weights
